citations.review_text: Wouldn't recommend when you got a modern PC parts. It freezes randomly on battles or randomly in the game. Even thought i barely got hours on it the gameplay was good but its ruined by the constant freezing not even crashing it just stays frozen until I have to forcefully shut down/
great game still fun to play after this many years only slight problem with battels causing the game to crash sometimes

claims.claim: This cohort reports that the game has a learning curve for newcomers to the series, though a tutorial prologue is available to help learn mechanics.

citations.review_text: A bit of a learning curve for a nwbie to the ip. But great fun when thats done.

Some say performance is bad but on my laptop (with integrated graphics, not even a gaming pc) if you put the important stuff (in terms of graphics setting like unit details and texture filtering, anti-aliasing slows it down quite a bit) it runs well. Loading times aren't bad with workshop mods either. The game itself is decent, if you are new to total war the prologue is good to learn the mechanics. As always (especially with CA) there are some things lacking but if you are interested in the period and your computer cant run attila then this is a good game

This game is one of the best historical strategy games I've ever played and there's so much detail to keep me invested. I dived in with no prior TW experience and after about four hours I started to get the hang of coordinating the controls and issuing orders on the battlefield, the whole experience is worth getting past the learning curve!

citations.review_text:
Total War Rome II - the game that the community either refuses to call a total war game, or are completely loyal to the game.

I am of the completely loyal fanbase.

Total War Rome II isn't for everyone (OBVIOUSLY) - you have to plan your economy, manage multiple fronts, manage politics and your subjects happiness, and MOST importantly - you are going to have to learn that losing is just part of the experience.

Every campaign you do is different. Some games everyone cowers before you and you decimate and conquer without hardly any resistance, and other games it feels like the entire world is out to get you.

Funnily enough the main complaint I always see or hear is how slow things progress, whether its troop movement, or combat itself. And to that I say to you, this is swords, armor, catapults, and overall mashing troops into troops combat. There are no guns, no tanks, no air support. The only way to guarantee a quick victory is with deep strategizing and outflanking.

Listen, as far as I am concerned, this scratches my RTS itch and my Roman Empire itch. I am hopelessly addicted and likely will be a while.

THAT ALL SAID, the game is not perfect, and there are things I hope to be added if a Rome III ever is released.

1 - Being able to trade/buy/sell/transfer land to allies. It is beyond frustrating that you are forced to conquer land and have no option to give your subjects or allies more land.

2 - Carthage. Plain and simple. They need to be seriously reworked because as it stands the developers absolutely did them dirty. Carthage had a very real chance of winning the first and even the second punic wars, but in Rome II, they are horrendous to play. They have zero economy, and much worse units than both Rome and the Syracuse who will both declare war on you sometimes within the first turn. More often than not you get obliterated, and I had to download mods just to make them playable, and even then its very 50/50 whether you will get a good game or…

I love the game but there is so many things that they could change, Ik its old but when i declare war i don't need my client states joining the other side, as well as not being able to give away cities. And multiplayer sometimes just crashes for no reason. Great game that i will continue to play just a few things i dislike

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players praise the vast faction variety while highlighting bugs, crashes, and frustrating political mechanics that require mods.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the political and civil war mechanics, particularly managing party loyalty and handling secessions from creating invasion armies, as frustrating and requiring mods to fix or bypass.

citations.review_text: everytime I create armies to invade someone I get secession and I have to fight the armies that I've created, this is so frustrating.. and I can't understand how can my General die like when I have 100 men out of his unit still alive, this is dumb...

Rome 2 (with Divide et Impera mod) is the definitive total war experience. While the base game is a bit too casual and might as well reward random clicking on lower difficulties, DEI adds layers of immersion, trade-offs and complexity that make your choices meaningful (instead of just receiving infinity buffs and bonuses like the base-game without trade-offs).

DEI battles can be a slog, but provide far more tactical nuance than the base game. You can add sub mods to bring the battle duration closer to the base game if time is a factor.

The supply and area of recruitment systems mean you have to plan your moves and buildings carefully. Politics is essentially a means to avoid civil wars or deal with them efficiently when they inevitably arise. There's a decent amount of depth to character and family management, which is good.

As with every total war game, siege battles are atrocious. Do not play them unless you like a buggy mess.

And if you're bored with DEI, you can always try out several other overhaul mods which transport you to different eras, introduce different mechanics and all the rest of it.

Without fail, I keep coming back to Rome 2 year after year, month after month. The franchise completely fell apart with the saga titles, but older titles are more alive than ever because of mods. 

Modern CA is not a good games studio (punto e basta), but their older games up until Attila were good, even though campaign mechanics from R1 were progressively removed for some odd reason.

If ancient warfare, conquest and empire expansion is up your alley, Rome 2 Divide et Impera is for you. Try it.
just love this game and alot off the other total wars tho not as keen on the dodgey civil mechanic its so so bogus so using mods is a must to negate this BS n makes game super fun too

Awesome military strategy game. It makes you feel like you are a general on the field with your army. Only recommendation is i wish they would rework/ allow you to edit the party loyalty system. I just want to fight wars on very hard without having to worry about my rear provinces rising up into civil war.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game features a large variety of playable factions, contributing to replay value.

citations.review_text: Rome II has come a long way since its rough launch. The scale of the battles is still impressive, and building an empire across the campaign map is incredibly satisfying. There are plenty of factions to try, which gives the game great replay value.
very fun and many different playable factions

Love this game, one of my favorite of the franchise. plenty of playable nations, and different (enough) units and start points to make it nearly infinitely replayable. End game is a bit slow, but i feel like that just comes with the territory. 9/10

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game suffers from technical issues, crashes, or bugs that become more apparent with extended play or on newer systems.

citations.review_text: NOT SURE WHY THIS GAME KEEPS CRASHING UPON STARTUP WITH NO MODS RUNNING.

I play almost exclusively with mods for this game. DEI mod has brought my love back to the game after years away. while the AI is not good. I handicap myself by playing as "realistic" as possible. move the armies how i think the character's leading them would and all that. Its a game where you can create your own narrative for the ups and downs of your civilization. Have fun with the large variety of units. 
overall it is a fun game that is filled with bugs which are more apparent the more you play. however it is still one of my favourites.

In my opinion TW Rome 2 is an Incredible game that aged very well.
The game does have issues on newer systems but the upcoming Update will hopefully fix the issues. 

> Great Graphics

> Fun Gameplay

>Good Replayability

>Large modding community

My Favourite Total War Game and I highly recommend it for those looking to get into Total War!

<3
